summary: Experimental psychedelic-assisted therapy using N,N-dimethyltryptamine (DMT), a short-acting psychedelic. Studies are exploring whether it could help depression, anxiety, addiction and distress at the end of life; it is only available in research studies.
description: DMT is a strong, fast-acting psychedelic that acts on serotonin. It is found naturally in plants and in small amounts in the human body. In research studies, DMT is given into a vein or a muscle and causes an intense but short psychedelic experience (5–30 minutes). Early clinical and laboratory studies suggest it may quickly affect mood and the brain's ability to form new connections, which could one day make it a new treatment for mental health conditions. In these studies, DMT is paired with therapy, preparation and integration. Because its effects are so short compared with psilocybin or LSD, researchers are interested in whether it could be easier to use in a clinic. It is still being studied, is not FDA-approved, and is only available in research studies.

evidence.overall_level_original: Early-phase clinical trials and preclinical evidence
evidence.research_support: Multiple ongoing studies exploring DMT in depression and addiction treatment.

typical_course.display: Single or multiple sessions within structured therapy

session_duration.display: 5–30 minutes (psychedelic experience), with 1–2 hours preparation and integration

safety.overall_safety: Generally well tolerated in controlled settings; because it starts and wears off quickly, the risk of long-lasting effects is lower. Risks include short-term anxiety, fast heartbeat, high blood pressure, dissociation (feeling detached from yourself or your surroundings) and possible emotional distress.

serious_risks.risk: Triggering psychotic episode in vulnerable individuals

contraindications.contraindication: History of schizophrenia or psychotic disorders
Taking medicines that raise serotonin (risk of serotonin syndrome: too much serotonin causing agitation, fever, shaking, fast heartbeat — get urgent help)

details.procedure_type: Intravenous DMT, Intramuscular DMT, Inhaled DMT (experimental)
details.session_protocol:
Administration of IV or IM DMT in a clinical/therapeutic environment
Acute monitoring during the 5–30 minute psychedelic state
Therapeutic support throughout the experience
Integration therapy session(s) following the psychedelic exposure

sections.text: DMT is a serotonergic psychedelic primarily acting as a 5-HT2A receptor agonist, with additional activity at 5-HT1A and sigma-1 receptors. Its rapid onset triggers profound alterations in consciousness, perception, and emotional processing. Preclinical evidence suggests DMT enhances neuroplasticity, synaptogenesis, and stress resilience. In therapy, the psychedelic state may facilitate breakthroughs in cognition, emotional regulation, and therapeutic alliance.

long_term: Sustained antidepressant effects in some patients

rare: Triggering psychotic episode in vulnerable individuals

absolute: History of schizophrenia or psychotic disorders
relative: Use of serotonergic medications (risk of serotonin syndrome)

ideal_candidates: Patients in palliative care with end-of-life anxiety
Individuals with substance use disorders in structured programs

studies: Phase I/II trials of IV DMT in depression showing safety and preliminary efficacy.
Preclinical studies showing rapid-acting antidepressant-like effects of DMT.
Comparisons with ayahuasca studies demonstrating potential for mood and addiction improvements.
sections.limitations: Limited sample sizes; short follow-up durations; optimal protocols (dose, frequency) not yet established.

sections.total_treatment_cost: Projected to be moderate-to-high due to clinical monitoring
